sentence: A 38-year-old male patient was referred to the Nutrition Unit due to chylous ascites.
His previous history highlighted the presence of smoking and repeated renal colic.
8 months before coming to our clinic he was diagnosed with left testicular seminoma with retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy (stage II C).
He underwent surgery with a left radical orchiectomy.
He subsequently received chemotherapy treatment with the BEP protocol (3 cycles of Bleomycin-Cisplatin-Etoposide and a fourth cycle of Cisplatin-Etoposide).

After chemotherapy, a significant decrease in the size of the lymphadenopathy mass was observed (4.2 x 3 cm in its maximum diameter versus 11 x 6 cm initially), but given the persistence of the lymphadenopathy, it was decided to perform retroperitoneal lymphadenectomy.
This intervention occurred without complications in the immediate postoperative period, but three weeks after surgery he consulted due to abdominal pain and distension.
His physical examination revealed a distended, hard, diffusely painful abdomen with signs of ascites.
Significant ascites was observed in the abdominal ultrasound.
In the abdominal computed tomography, post-surgical changes from retroperitoneal lymphadenectomy and a significant amount of intra-abdominal free fluid were detected.

Evacuation paracentesis was performed with extraction of 8,000 cc of milky-looking ascitic fluid; The analysis of said fluid showed: leukocytes 508/mm3, Polymorphonuclear cells 14%, Mononuclear cells 86%, triglycerides 875 mg/dl.
Tumor origin was ruled out because necrosis and calcification were identified in the resected lymph nodes and the tumor markers (AFP and HCG) were negative.
Three evacuating paracenteses were performed weekly, extracting 3, 7 and 4 liters successively.
In the Nutrition Consultation, the patient reported moderate asthenia with a feeling of early postprandial fullness.

The physical examination revealed weight 66 kg, height 177 cm, ideal weight 79.2 kg, BMI 21.06, triceps fold 12 mm (91.8% p50), arm muscle circumference 21.8 cm (89% p50). , BP 115/71 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, normal cardiopulmonary ascultation and no signs of pleural effusion and abdominal examination without relevant findings.

The analytical assessment showed: glucose 92 mg/dl (60-100), creatinine 1.2 mg/dl (0.8-1.3), urate 7.9 mg/dl (3.5-7.2), Normal Na, K, Cl, Calcium and phosphorus, normal liver profile, total cholesterol 233 mg/dl (HDL 52 mg/dl, LDL 153 mg/dl), triglycerides 152 mg/dl (< 150), total proteins 6.4 g/dl (6.6-8.3), albumin 3.3 g/dl (3.5-5.2), Fe 63 μg/dl (70-180), ferritin 265 ng/ml (20-400 ), transferin saturation 25% (15-40), transferrin 201 mg/dl (200-360), red blood cells 4,860,000/μl (4,400,000-5,800,000), hemoglobin 14.3 g/dl (13-17, 3), MCV 87.2 fl (80-97), hematocrit 42.4% (38.9-51.4), leukocytes 6,760/μl (3,700-11,600), lymphocytes 830/μl (800-3,000), polymorphonuclear cells 5,250/μl (1,000- 5,400), rest of normal white series, platelets 501,000/μl (125,000-350,000), prothrombin activity 89% (75-120), vitamin B12, 422 pg/ml (197-866), folate 7.7 ng/ml (3.1-17.5), zinc 52 μg/dl, vitamin A/retinol binding protein 0.8 (0.8-1.2), vitamin E/cholesterol 6 (6-12), vitamin D 35 ng/ml (30-100), PTH 33 pg/ml (12-65), B-HCG < 1 mIU/ml (0-5), AFP 3.32 ng/ml (0-16).
The patient was diagnosed with mild protein-calorie malnutrition in the context of chylous ascites secondary to retroperitoneal lymphadenectomy.

A high protein diet was started with fat restriction and divided into 5-6 daily meals along with MCT 20 ml daily, zinc sulfate 1 tablet daily, a multivitamin complex and 100 grams daily of a specific supplement enriched in MCT.
This supplement provides 424 kcal and 11.4 grams of protein per 100 grams.

With this therapeutic approach the patient only required an evacuating paracentesis and 3 months later he presented the following anthropometric data: weight 70.1 kg, triceps fold 13 mm (100% p50), arm muscle circumference 23 cm (93% p50) ; Previously altered analytical parameters were also normalized.
